issues.title: Claim is not atomic across workers
issues.explanation: A plain SELECT followed by UPDATE lets two workers read the same queued row before either commits, so both run the job. Nothing locks the row or re-checks its status in the UPDATE.
issues.fix: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in the same transaction as the UPDATE, or a single UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING.

issues.title: Job gets one attempt too many
issues.explanation: attempts counts finished tries. After the 5th failure attempts == 5, which is not > 5, so the job is queued a 6th time. JOBS-77 says MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts in total.

issues.title: Success is re-run when complete() fails
issues.explanation: complete() sits inside the same try as the handler. If the handler sent the email and the UPDATE or commit then fails, the except path calls fail() and requeues a job that already succeeded. The connection is also left in an aborted transaction with no rollback, so fail() itself raises and kills the worker.
issues.fix: Run only the handler inside the try; call db.rollback() before fail(); handle complete() errors separately.

issues.title: Unknown job kind crashes the worker loop
issues.explanation: HANDLERS[...] is outside the try. A kind the worker does not know yet raises KeyError, the process dies and the job stays 'running'. After the visibility timeout another worker claims it and dies too; reclaiming does not bump attempts, so it never reaches 'dead'.
issues.fix: Look up the handler inside the try (or fail the job explicitly) and count reclaims as attempts.

issues.title: Invoice email handler is not idempotent
issues.explanation: The queue is at-least-once: a crash or failure after send() but before complete() retries the job. The handler never checks emailed_at and passes no idempotency_key, so the customer gets the email again.
issues.fix: Return early if invoice.emailed_at is set and pass idempotency_key=f"invoice-{invoice.id}" to send().
